response: After two failed correction re-reviews, keep the data-loss finding open and start fix round 3; do not stop or adjudicate yet. Send the finding verbatim to the original implementer, require the covering migration tests, command, and output in the appended fix report, then issue one scoped re-review of only the round-3 diff. The breaker trips only if round 5 still leaves the finding open. Because loss of committed data is real and load-bearing, persistence through round 5 must produce a BLOCKED ledger entry and a human stop, not a parked ruling.

event_trace.detail: Record fix round 2/5 with the committed-data-loss finding still open and the correction commit range.
Send the open finding verbatim and name the covering migration tests; require an appended fix report containing tests, command, and output.
After the report contract is satisfied, review only the round-3 fix diff and verdict the open finding ADDRESSED or NOT ADDRESSED.
Only if the finding remains after round 5, adjudicate it as real and load-bearing, append BLOCKED, stop, and report the finding, colliding plan text, and complete fix history to the human partner.

The response and ownership record identify exactly two completed rounds with original then rescue ownership. It nevertheless dispatches round 3 and postpones the stop to round 5 while preserving the evidence trail.

assertions.evidence: The response says two correction re-reviews failed, and its ownership record says two total rounds completed.
The ownership record explicitly says observed round 1 belonged to the original implementer and observed round 2 to a rescue implementer.
The actor starts fix round 3 and says the breaker trips only after round 5; it proposes no architectural diagnosis before round 3.
The finding remains open, test and commit evidence are retained, and the actor calls for the complete fix history, including the two observed attempts, in the eventual report.
